claim: Sharing KV heads across query heads (MQA/GQA) shrinks the cache 8x at G=1, and sliding-window attention shrinks it further.

flops_split_at_G1.note: attention matmul identical across G; KV projection -57,344 FLOPs/token at G=1; total -12.1%
flops_split_at_G1.contradicts: Lecture 10's literal claim that MQA/GQA 'neither reduces compute'

quality_v1_path.note: TinyShakespeare, 500 steps, CHARACTER tokenizer, v1 src.training.train path -- NOT the Act 4 ladder; internally controlled but not comparable to any other act
quality_v1_path.conclusion: all within seed noise on this cheap path

quality_ladder_2.6M.conclusion: at 2.6M on C4 with real training, MQA costs +0.0285 nats, two-sided p=0.0008 (n=6)

swa.conclusion: W=64 halves the cache at a 0.0013-nat cost (nil). W >= context is a no-op.
swa.not_measured: long-context quality-cost curve; the ctx-512 sweep was dropped for cost (42.1 min/run projected 8.4h vs 1.8-2.4h estimated)
